fact_check.claim: CAMP charges $295 per semester
fact_check.note: Page says a single cost of $295 per semester for undergraduates. Also on academicmaterials.cornell.edu and /how-it-works.

fact_check.claim: CAMP is for undergraduate students taking undergraduate courses; fee set in advance; required materials only
fact_check.note: Page says undergraduates taking undergraduate courses, cost set upfront, required textbooks and coursepacks.

fact_check.claim: Fee appears on July Bursar statement for fall and January statement for spring
fact_check.note: FAQ says exactly this.

fact_check.claim: Digital first; print only when no digital option exists
fact_check.note: FAQ: digital is default, print only when no digital option.

fact_check.claim: Ebooks open in Canvas under the Course Materials tab; print picked up at The Cornell Store
fact_check.note: Course Materials tab in Canvas confirmed; the Cornell Store pickup location was not in the FAQ text I retrieved.

fact_check.claim: Must be fully enrolled in a course to receive materials; students studying abroad are not enrolled that semester
fact_check.note: FAQ supports both (waitlisted students get nothing; study abroad semesters are not enrolled), but the article gives no source link for this bullet.

fact_check.claim: Print kept if you stay in; if you opt out or drop, return in like-new condition within 14 days or pay retail
fact_check.note: FAQ: return print in like-new condition within 14 days of opting out to avoid bursar charges. 'Pay the retail price' wording not confirmed beyond 'bursar charges'; 'drop the course' not confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Students saved an estimated $2.88 million combined, about $145 per student per semester in the first year
fact_check.note: Article reports an estimated $2.88 million and about $145 per student per semester.

fact_check.claim: Program FAQ cites an average of $140 per semester
fact_check.note: FAQ estimates $140 average savings per semester in the first year.

fact_check.claim: Opt out via CAMP email link or Canvas Course Materials tab, Opt-Out in top right corner
fact_check.note: Supported by the FAQ, but steps 1 and 2 in the numbered list carry no source link.

fact_check.claim: Confirmation email within 24 hours; otherwise write to textbooks@cornell.edu
fact_check.note: FAQ says confirmation within 24 hours, contact textbooks@cornell.edu if none (no inline link in article, covered by the step 1-2 fix).

fact_check.claim: Fee reversed on bursar account in 5 to 7 business days
fact_check.note: FAQ: 5-7 business days.

fact_check.claim: Fall 2026 opt-out deadline was September 11, 2026
fact_check.note: FAQ gives September 11, 2026 for fall.

fact_check.claim: How-it-works page lists a $295 charge on the January statement and points to an Important Dates page; no spring 2027 date posted
fact_check.note: Page shows $295 flat rate, January statement, Important Dates tab, no date given in the text.

fact_check.claim: Late requests reviewed individually and may be denied without a valid academic reason
fact_check.note: FAQ says so.

fact_check.claim: Re-enrolling after the deadline carries a $295 charge
fact_check.note: FAQ supports it ($295 charge to bursar account on opt-in after deadline by email), but the sentence has no source link.

fact_check.claim: Financial aid does not require staying in; aid is based on a cost of attendance that includes an estimate for books and supplies; bursar balance may remain
fact_check.note: FAQ confirms you need not stay in CAMP to keep aid and a balance may remain; the cost-of-attendance books-and-supplies wording was not in the retrieved text. Sentence has no inline link.

fact_check.claim: $620 per semester national average
fact_check.note: Page cites $620 per semester nationwide.

fact_check.claim: Passananti '25 said he spent less than $250 per semester; peers about $100 to $200
fact_check.note: Sun reports both. Student voice used as attributed experience, not as a hard fact, so acceptable.

fact_check.claim: Xi Wang '24 said she assumed most people would compare cost of books to the flat fee
fact_check.note: Sun says Wang expected students to compare book cost with the $225 fee, but the source text I retrieved gives no pronoun. 'She' and 'assumed' are not supported; also omit that Wang is a Cornell Store student employee, which matters for attribution.

fact_check.claim: Brian Young, Cornell Store academic materials manager, suggested students check whether their subjects would benefit
fact_check.note: Sun: the committee noted some disciplines have lower costs, so students can check whether courses would benefit.

fact_check.claim: That story was written when the fee was $225
fact_check.note: Flat $225 per semester, opt out by Sept. 9.

fact_check.claim: Store no longer houses in-stock textbooks; opted-out students can special-order print from the textbook help desk
fact_check.note: Both stated.

fact_check.claim: Store page tells graduate students to compare prices with other online retailers
fact_check.note: Stated.

fact_check.claim: Buffalo Street Books: no 7% NYS sales tax and free delivery to Cornell classes (2013)
fact_check.note: Feb 6, 2013 article says this; article correctly flags it as old. Student-voice/newspaper source for a current fee claim is only acceptable because it is hedged.

fact_check.claim: Bookstore buyback typically returns only 10 to 25 percent of original value
fact_check.note: Quote came from the Ithaca Book Trade co-founder, not a bookstore; article says 'bookstore buyback'. Reword to attribute it to the site's co-founder.

fact_check.claim: Student-run exchange sites mentioned in the 2013 piece
fact_check.note: It describes Ithaca Book Trade, an Ithaca College-only site at the time; relevance to Cornell is weak.

fact_check.claim: Instant Access Program provides digital textbooks and publisher software for participating graduate and professional courses in Canvas; select titles at reduced rates, opt-in
fact_check.note: Both pages confirm.

fact_check.claim: CAMP does not cover graduate students; grad courses taken by undergrads are outside CAMP and you pay extra fees yourself
fact_check.note: Grad students not covered is confirmed; the 'you pay any extra fees yourself' consequence was not in the retrieved text.

fact_check.claim: Course reserves hold items at the circulation desk for short-term loan, instructors request them; okureserve@cornell.edu
fact_check.note: Stated.

fact_check.claim: 2018 pilot: textbook reserve requests; loans typically 2 hours, anyone with current Cornell ID
fact_check.note: Page (header 2018, posted Dec 4, 2019) says typically 2 hours and any current Cornell ID. Article correctly says pilot status is unconfirmed.

fact_check.claim: Many digital textbooks have extended access of up to 5 years
fact_check.note: Stated.

fact_check.claim: Store's textbooks page does not mention rentals
fact_check.note: Confirmed. Note the Store's separate textbook-buyback page still exists (content stale, spring 2020) and says to contact textbooks@cornell.edu.

beats_top.query: cornell textbooks cheap where to buy used ithaca
beats_top.why: The #1 result is a roughly 2006 Sun story on Cornell Store versus Kraftees prices and says nothing about CAMP, so ours answers the question with current numbers, the deadline and a by-situation table. It is thin on actual used-book sources, which is the literal query.
changes: Add one or two currently verifiable used or rental options for opted-out undergrads and grad students (for example the Cornell Store's textbook-buyback page and whether a used-book shop in Collegetown or downtown still operates), each linked to its own current page, or state plainly that none could be confirmed.
Source every hard fact inline (study-abroad/enrollment rule, opt-out steps, $295 re-enroll charge, financial aid sentence).

fixes: In the bullet 'You must be fully enrolled in a course to receive its materials, and students studying abroad are not enrolled that semester', add the inline link https://academicmaterials.cornell.edu/frequently-asked-questions and also say waitlisted students do not receive materials.

In 'How to opt out', add the inline link https://academicmaterials.cornell.edu/frequently-asked-questions to step 1 (CAMP email link or Canvas Course Materials tab, Opt-Out in top right) and step 2 (confirmation within 24 hours, textbooks@cornell.edu).

Link the sentence 'Re-enrolling after the deadline carries a $295 charge' to https://academicmaterials.cornell.edu/frequently-asked-questions and say you request opt-in by email to textbooks@cornell.edu after the deadline.

In the financial aid paragraph, add an inline link to https://academicmaterials.cornell.edu/frequently-asked-questions and delete 'aid is based on a cost of attendance that includes an estimate for books and supplies' unless you can quote the FAQ wording; keep: you do not have to stay in CAMP to keep your aid, and a bursar balance may remain after reversal.

In the Daily Sun paragraph, change 'Xi Wang '24 said she assumed most people would compare' to 'Xi Wang '24, a Cornell Store student employee, expected students to compare the cost of the books they need with the fee' (drop the pronoun and 'assumed'); source https://cornellsun.com/2022/07/24/what-you-need-to-know-about-cornells-new-academic-materials-program/.

In the Peer sales bullet, change 'bookstore buyback typically returns only 10 to 25 percent' to say that the co-founder of the Ithaca Book Trade site said a textbook typically returns only 10 to 25 percent of its original value at the end of the semester; also say that site served only Ithaca College students at the time, or delete the peer-sales bullet.
In the graduate section, remove 'you pay any extra fees for it yourself' unless it is linked to FAQ text saying so; keep only that graduate and professional courses are outside CAMP.

Under 'Where to find cheap used books if you opt out', add the Cornell Store's textbook-buyback page (https://www.cornellstore.com/textbook-buyback) with the caveat that its text still reflects spring 2020 and to email textbooks@cornell.edu for current buyback terms, or add one other currently verifiable used or rental source with its own link.
